Hi Jordan / Emily,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through Acme's search/ranking goals. Quick recap and next steps on our side:

- Goal: Improve search relevance for product support articles and knowledge base with a reranker that reorders candidate results from your existing retrieval layer.
- Key success metrics you mentioned: mean reciprocal rank (MRR) improvement, top-3 precision, and reduction in manual escalations for KB answers.

Technical follow-ups we promised:
1) SDK & auth: Simple steps to wire up the Redwood SDK and API keys for a sandbox project.
2) Ranking API & top_k: how to call the re-rank endpoint vs using embeddings/rerank locally and recommended top_k defaults.
3) Structured output/tool calling: how to use structured JSON outputs for downstream routing (intent, confidence, actions).
4) Eval templates: we shared a CSV template for labeled pairs + relevance judgments you can use to run offline evals.

Attached: reranker-eval-templates.csv (labeling template), redwood-reranker-arch.png (example routing + fallback).

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the eval template with ~200 representative queries and candidate result sets (due: 7/6).
- We provide a sandbox key + integration guide and a 30-min tech hang for your eng team (can we do Wed 7/1 or Thu 7/2?).
- If the offline eval looks promising, run a small A/B with a single route and report top-3 precision baseline vs reranker.

Looping in Dev Patel (infra) and Marcus Lin (solutions) — they'll help with the SDK sample and evaluation checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A few clarifying Qs from our side so we can prep the template: 

1) When you say 'rerank endpoint' — is that a synchronous API we call per query? What's the expected P95 latency for top_k=10? We need to size our latency budget (target P95 <= 250ms).

2) For eval labels: should we label binary relevant/not-relevant or graded relevance (0/1/2)? We have mixed labeling capacity.

3) Auth: we prefer short-lived keys tied to a service account. Can you support token-based service accounts (OIDC exchange) or only API keys?

4) If we want to preserve the existing retrieval layer but only rerank candidates, do you recommend sending embeddings for the candidates or just tokenized text?

Also Wed 7/1 at 11:00am PT works for a 30-min tech hang (we'll confirm internally).

—Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reranker integration: follow-up + evaluation questions

Perfect — Dev and Marcus will pick this up. Quick answers below and we'll expand during the tech hang: 

1) Rerank endpoint & latency:
- We offer a synchronous /v1/rerank endpoint: you POST candidates + query, receive an ordered list with scores.
- Typical P95 depends on model/instance; for our medium open-source reranker on dedicated infra P95 ~ 120-220ms for top_k=10. We'll include a recommended hardware profile for your QPS target.

2) Labels for eval:
- Graded relevance (0,1,2) is ideal for richer metrics (nDCG), but binary (0/1) is fine if labeling bandwidth is limited. The attached CSV supports either — column "grade" can be 0/1/2.

3) Auth options:
- We support API keys out of the box for sandbox. For production we support short‑lived tokens via OIDC service account exchange and can integrate with your IdP. We'll send the service-account onboarding doc.

4) Candidate inputs:
- Reranker works best when you send raw text for candidates plus optional precomputed embeddings. If you already have embeddings, include them to save inference; otherwise send text and let Redwood compute embeddings under the hood.

Dev/Marcus — can you provide the SDK snippet (Node + Python) and an example request payload (top_k param, return_structured=true) before the Wed hang?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Hi Jordan — quick tech notes and a sample: 

Sample Node call (excerpt):
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>
Body (JSON): {
  "query": "How do I reset my account password?",
  "candidates": [ { "id": "c1", "text": "..." }, { "id": "c2", "text": "..." } ],
  "top_k": 10,
  "return_structured": true
}

Response (partial):
[ { "id": "c2", "score": 0.92, "metadata": { "intent": "reset_password", "confidence": 0.88 } }, ... ]

Notes:
- top_k: start with 10 for offline eval. For production, many customers use top_k=20 for rerank then truncate downstream to top-3 for UI.
- structured outputs: set return_structured=true to receive an action/intent field. We recommend validating intent schemas in advance.
- batching: to hit your latency SLO, use small concurrent batches and prefer dedicated capacity for consistent P95.

I'll attach a short checklist in the drive link for what we need from your side (queries, candidates, any precomputed embeddings).

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
